Sorted gaps decompose every original edge difference and induce rank-level cuts; summing supplies the \(h_k\) lower bound. Two-level vectors attain every ratio. Centered-edge cut profiles are proved for all finite sizes and cross-checked with 72 exact-rational parameter cases; a standalone checker completed 140,414 exact tests. General proof, not testing, supports the infinite family. Flat convex densities are handled by choosing a positive gap with \(\Phi(a)>0\).

value.rationale: A common sharp invariant across every convex Orlicz-type graph edge energy is a meaningful rearrangement stability property, not just a single numerical norm. The structural cardinality-cut formula gives actual extremizers and characterizes precisely when sorted data decrease every such energy. Symmetric central conductance defects exhibit a parity-dependent sharp lower threshold: even paths stay contractive as the defect vanishes, while odd paths have unbounded amplification. This naturally tests robustness of weighted Pólya–Szegő smoothing on inhomogeneous finite chains. The result is deliberately restricted to one-input energy, not presented as a new two-point estimate.
